rac1/pal.label: Preview a level in OpenRAC Editor
rac1/pal.description: Opens one extracted level in OpenRAC Editor's player, to fly around it. This is OpenRAC Editor showing the editor's scene, not the game.

rac1/pal.label: Extract the levels
rac1/pal.description: Turns the 19 levels on your disc into OpenRAC Editor projects, one per level, in your levels folder. About 20 seconds and 800 MB. Run it again to add levels or bring them up to date: levels you edited are kept, and one made by an older editor is backed up with your edits before it is written again.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS the same command wrote the per-level projects, and refused an existing folder with a clear message.

rac1/pal.label: Export the levels again
rac1/pal.description: Reads every level from your disc into its OpenRAC Editor project again, even one that is up to date. The levels there now go to a backups folder first, and the objects you moved, changed, added or deleted are carried onto the fresh ones (Ratchet & Clank); anything that cannot be carried is listed, to redo by hand.

rac1/pal.label: Import a level into OpenRAC Editor
rac1/pal.description: Has OpenRAC Editor read one level's meshes and textures without opening a window. Not needed before opening the editor, which does the same the first time (a few seconds per level).
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS, the editor imported one extracted level this way in five seconds.

rac1/pal.label: Open a level in OpenRAC Editor
rac1/pal.description: Opens one level in OpenRAC Editor: move, turn or scale its objects and save. Each level is a project of its own, so only that level loads.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. The project file is assets/godot/project.godot, as the action expects.

rac1/pal.label: Pack your edited levels
rac1/pal.description: Turns the levels you edited in OpenRAC Editor back into the game's level data, in your packed levels folder; your disc image is never changed. Packs the objects you moved, turned, scaled, changed, added or deleted.
rac1/pal.todo: Run from a shell on macOS: an untouched project packs to nothing, a scene Godot re-saved with one object moved packs to a level file that differs from the disc in that object's record, and the port ran level 0 for 400 frames from it. Not run from the desktop app yet. Next: adding and deleting objects, then ties and shrubs.

rac1/pal.label: Add as a new planet
rac1/pal.description: Packs the level you pick and adds it to your mods as a new planet the ship can fly to. The original planet stays as it is. Name the planet in OpenRAC Editor first (Project > Project Settings > OpenRAC > Planet). Adding it again updates the same planet.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. In a Linux container the same command packed Aridia with Ratchet moved and a model added, added it to an overrides folder, and the PAL port played the new planet from its own files (started on it directly; the ship's menu was not driven there).

rac1/pal.label: Show your textures in the editor
rac1/pal.description: Puts the textures of the mods you put together (Put the mods together) into the level editor's projects, at their own size, so that the levels you edit in OpenRAC Editor look as they will in the game. The editor's own come back with Hide them again.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS a 4x terrain texture showed at its size in the editor after the import.

rac1/pal.label: Hide your textures in the editor
rac1/pal.description: Puts the level editor's own textures back in its projects, in place of the mods' (Show your textures in the editor).
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS a 4x terrain texture showed at its size in the editor after the import.
